slides.0.title: Why Study Australian Wine?
slides.0.subtitle: Level 1 · Module 1 · Lesson 1
slides.1.title: Australia's Place in the Global Wine Market
slides.1.points.0: 5th largest wine exporter globally (2023 export value: A$1.8 billion)
slides.1.points.1: Approximately 145,000 hectares under vine across 6 states + territories
slides.1.points.3: Annual production: ~1.3 billion bottles, with 70% exported
slides.1.points.4: Top export markets: UK, USA, China, Canada
slides.1.note: Although Australia is a New World wine country, its winemaking history dates back to 1788 with British colonisation
slides.2.title: Six Defining Characteristics of Australian Wine
slides.2.points.0: 🌡️ Diverse climates: from cool maritime Tasmania to hot continental Barossa — an enormous spectrum
slides.2.points.1: 🍇 Variety of grapes: from Shiraz, Cabernet and Chardonnay to Italian and Portuguese varieties
slides.2.points.2: 🔩 Technical innovation: pioneer of the Stelvin screwcap closure, world leader in winemaking technology
slides.2.points.3: 🌱 Sustainable viticulture: organic and biodynamic farming growing fast; Bush vine old-vine preservation
slides.2.points.4: 🏆 Outstanding value: from everyday supermarket wines to world-class collectibles — wide price range
slides.2.points.5: 🌏 Cultural fusion: diverse European immigrant traditions — Italian, German and French influences coexist
slides.3.question: What is Australia's rank among global wine exporters?
slides.3.explanation: Australia is the world's 5th largest wine exporter. Its primary markets are the UK, USA and China.
slides.4.title: Lesson Summary
slides.4.points.0: Australia is a major wine exporting nation — annual exports worth A$1.8 billion
slides.4.points.1: Spans multiple climate zones; remarkable diversity of varieties and styles
slides.4.points.2: Renowned for technological innovation (screwcap) and outstanding value for money
